Don't put a heater inside the beehive. Bees need to regulate themselves. You can wrap them in insulation, if you want.

I catch a lot of swarms. Maybe you will too. Have you read the pdf about bait hives from cornell university? http://ecommons.cornell.edu/bitstream/handle/1813/2653/Bait%20Hives%20for%20Honey%20Bees.pdf;jsessionid=AB63DE731822C0382EE94F0C0830EF58?sequence=2

I understand they need to regulate their own heat, but assumed adding a heater decently below their normal temperature might help them out when they really need it. I prefer the idea of insulating the hive, so I might just go that way. Maybe just some sort of wrap or external cover that won't disrupt ventilation or movement that I can add on as winter approaches.

I hadn't seen that PDF, thanks for the link! I was worried that it might be hard to catch swarms these days with all the bee colonies dying off, so it's good to hear there are people out there still catching them.

One of the reasons I've read for not providing additional heat is this:

You will NEVER be able to get it as spot on as they can - which means this - * They have to compensate for hot spots, cools spots, and inaccuracies * You are introducing areas where pests may thrive * This may interfere with how they gauge their supplies and cause problems with spinning up too early for spring etc.

You feel good because they are warmer / have it easier - but you may be doing way more harm than help and interfering with much more than you intended.

Insulate and make it easier for them to do themselves - but don't think you can do it better than they can.
What you're saying makes sense to me, thanks for pointing that out. You are right, I was trying to make it easier for them, I didn't think about how it could mess things up.

I've read in the last few days that insulating the hive can be bad too, as it can cause condensation inside the hive and make it harder for the hive to warm up when there are warmer days. Wrapping the hive in black tar-paper seems to be preferred.

I guess staying simple is better!
